You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 3e1ad196385c65c1454aceab1226d9a4baca27d5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>
Date: Tue, 3 May 2022 17:35:25 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] btrfs: sysfs: export the balance paused state of exclusive
 operation

The new state allowing device addition with paused balance is not
exported to user space so it can't recognize it and actually start the
operation.

Fixes: efc0e69c2fea ("btrfs: introduce exclusive operation BALANCE_PAUSED state")
CC: stable@vger.kernel.org # 5.17
Signed-off-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>
---
 fs/btrfs/sysfs.c | 3 +++
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+)

diff --git a/fs/btrfs/sysfs.c b/fs/btrfs/sysfs.c
index 17389a42a3ab..ba78ca5aabbb 100644
--- a/fs/btrfs/sysfs.c
+++ b/fs/btrfs/sysfs.c
@@ -922,6 +922,9 @@ static ssize_t btrfs_exclusive_operation_show(struct kobject *kobj,
 		case BTRFS_EXCLOP_BALANCE:
 			str = "balance\n";
 			break;
+		case BTRFS_EXCLOP_BALANCE_PAUSED:
+			str = "balance paused\n";
+			break;
 		case BTRFS_EXCLOP_DEV_ADD:
 			str = "device add\n";
 			break;
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the lack of export of the "balance paused" state in the sysfs interface, which prevented user space from recognizing this state and starting the device addition operation while a balance operation was paused. This oversight occurred after the introduction of the exclusive operation BALANCE_PAUSED state, which was not reflected in the sysfs output.
